claims.text: As-solidified Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 contains several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases.
The as-solidified alloy contains only limited amorphous regions.
Conventional rapid cooling of this alloy produces extensive primary crystallization.
The alloy undergoes a multistep crystallization sequence during reheating.
A brief isothermal hold near the glass transition during rapid cooling promotes structural relaxation in the amorphous matrix.
The proposed structural relaxation reduces free volume.
The proposed structural relaxation inhibits atomic diffusion within the amorphous matrix.
Reduced atomic mobility suppresses primary crystallization.
The isothermal hold permits local atomic rearrangements that relax residual stresses.
A hold between Tg and crystallization onset can relax the glass without supplying sufficient energy for extensive crystal nucleation or growth.
Relative to continuous rapid cooling, the hold increases the retained amorphous volume fraction.
Relative to continuous rapid cooling, the hold shifts crystallization onset to a higher temperature during reheating.
The beneficial effect is confined to a narrow hold-temperature window between Tg and crystallization onset.
Hold temperatures outside that window may fail to inhibit crystallization effectively.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis calls the intervention a sub-Tg hold, whereas the intervention, conditions, and experimental design place the hold just above Tg and below crystallization onset. The experimental design also refers to this above-Tg treatment as a 'sub-Tg isothermal hold.'
